correctness.rationale: All four quantifier directions in the slice infimum formulas are preserved. For dc lower, for every normalized dual slice a Hölder norming pair (u,r) with |u|^p+r^p=1 can be realized by a scaled Daugavet-point fiber witness w whose norm approaches one and whose distance from x approaches two. The exact inequalities (b+r)^p≥b^p+r^p and |a-u|^p+r^p≥(1-a)^p force dc≥((1-a)^p+b^p)^(1/p). Concentrating scalar slices u→1 give equality. For Delta lower, every containing slice admits the same scalar coordinate a and a fiber witness near -x, giving 2b. For Delta upper, scalar slices u>a-η and the monotonic envelope |u-a|^p+(b+(1-u^p)^(1/p))^p≤(2b)^p for u≥a give a matching limit, with continuity for u<a. The a=0 and a=1 endpoints, strict gap for 0≤a<1, and full-sphere statement when every normalized Y-vector is Daugavet are explicitly derived.
risks: The finite verifier is illustrative, not a replacement for all-slice and real-exponent proofs.
The proof uses the genuine pointwise Daugavet assumption; it cannot be extended unchanged to arbitrary non-Daugavet fibers.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches and full-text implication comparisons identify the 2020 qualitative absolute-sum result, the 2023 defining quantitative stability paper, and three highly relevant exact published profiles. The old qualitative theorem gives a Delta-point locus but no pointwise constants. The closest indexed exact same-space pair of constants covers the different ball axis (t,0), not the mixed sphere (t,bx). Another exact result requires all components to be Daugavet spaces, which excludes a real scalar line; the atomic-summand formula is for p=1. Neither literature result implies the two sharp mixed-point identities. No covering mixed scalar–Daugavet two-constant statement was found among the inspected scientific claims.
residual_risks: Searches and these readings cannot prove absolute novelty: an equivalent mixed-sphere slice profile might exist under different terminology.
The argument does not assert quantitative universality for non-Daugavet fibers or p=1/infinity.
The 2020 qualitative Delta classification overlaps the zero-vs-nonzero qualitative locus; the accepted originality is specifically the simultaneous exact numerical two-constant profile and sharp gap.
risks: An independent literature audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves both natural local diameter-two radii for every unit vector of a scalar–Daugavet p-sum, with only a pointwise Daugavet hypothesis. It gives a nontrivial continuum-wide strict gap, an exact twofold Delta amplification relative to the previously known scalar-ball-axis value, and a complete Delta-locus and Daugavet-nonexistence classification when the second summand has the Daugavet property. This full mixed-sphere profile is not a routine restatement of qualitative inheritance or a random finite slice.
risks: The phenomenon is specific to one scalar atom and the strictly convex outer p range; further multiple-atom classifications are not claimed.
